comparison: Perfect agreement on study design claims (C1, C24-C25, C83-C88). Both evaluations find the longitudinal design, location, duration, participant numbers, and sampling strategy well-supported and clearly described.

Strong agreement on laboratory methods and data generation (C2-C3, C26-C30, C91-C95). Both evaluations praise the combination of barcodes and genome sequences as solid and well-described, with explicit sample numbers accepted.

Agreement on COI estimates and stability (C31-C36). Both accept the consistency across three methods and stable COI over time. OpenEval emphasizes statistical support (p<10⁻¹⁵), while peer review focuses on interpretation of constant transmission intensity (C60, C65).

Strong agreement on barcode validation against WGS (C37-C38, C63, C102). Both evaluations praise the strong correlation and agreement metrics. Peer review additionally emphasizes methodological insights (C59, C62, C103) that OpenEval addresses separately in R11.

Agreement on low inbreeding and extensive outcrossing (C4-C5, C39-C41, C64). Both accept evidence of continuous recombination and high genetic diversity. Peer review includes summary claim C57 that OpenEval evaluates separately in R16.
Agreement on rapid temporal decay of genetic relatedness (C42-C43, C70). Both accept the 10-fold decrease and strong statistical support as evidence of active recombination.

Agreement on household clustering (C6-C7, C44-C45, C78, C109). Both accept the sixfold difference and temporal limitation as evidence for household-level transmission, acknowledging this is an inference from spatial patterns.

Perfect agreement on seasonal effects (C8, C46, C58, C69). Both evaluations accept the fourfold difference during low-to-high transmission transition and the interpretation of increased diversity during peak transmission periods.

Divergent evaluations on drug resistance findings (C47-C52, C110-C111). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative DHPS A437G pattern and lack of statistical testing for seasonal changes. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, accepting the stability and seasonal patterns without methodological concerns.

Agreement on chronic infections (C9, C53-C56, C74). Both accept the 18-month infection case and duration range as well-documented evidence of persistent infections, without challenging the methodology.

Partial overlap on methodological insights (C59, C62). OpenEval groups these with policy recommendations (C60-C61, C67), while peer review evaluates them alongside barcode validation. Both accept the methodological claims as supported.

Partial overlap on active case detection rationale (C67). OpenEval includes this with methodological insights, while peer review groups it with policy recommendations (C81-C82, C108). Both accept the recommendation as well-supported.

Agreement on background and contextual claims (C22-C23, C66, C72-C73, C75). Both evaluations accept these cited claims as appropriate context. Peer review groups these with broader background literature (C10-C21, C68, C71, C76-C77, C79-C80) that OpenEval evaluates in R14.

Agreement on policy recommendations (C80-C82, C108). Both evaluations accept the recommendations for mass detection and household treatment as logical and well-supported by the study's findings on household clustering and asymptomatic reservoir.

Agreement on background literature claims (C10-C21, C68, C71, C76-C77, C79). Both evaluations accept these as appropriate context without challenge. Peer review includes additional contextual claims (C22-C23, C66, C72-C73, C75, C80) that OpenEval evaluates separately.

Agreement on methodological and ethical procedures (C89-C90, C101, C104-C107, C113-C114). Both evaluations accept these as adequately described and appropriate. Peer review includes additional methodological claims (C96-C100) that OpenEval evaluates in other results.

Agreement on summary conclusion (C57). OpenEval evaluates this separately as a synthesis of major findings, while peer review groups it with the underlying evidence on outcrossing and recombination. Both accept it as well-supported.
